findings.name: Property Tax Credit for 100% Disabled Veterans ("Circuit Breaker") and POW Full Homestead Exemption
findings.description: Missouri does not offer a broad property tax exemption for disabled veterans generally. Two distinct, narrower benefits are confirmed: (1) the Missouri Property Tax Credit ("circuit breaker") gives eligible resident veterans with a 100% VA service-connected disability rating a credit of up to $1,100/year for homeowners or $750/year for renters against real estate taxes or rent paid, subject to household income limits ($30,000 single / $34,000 married filing combined for full-year homeowners; $27,200 single / $29,200 married for renters and part-year owners); VA disability payments are excluded from the income calculation specifically for claimants who are 100% disabled as a result of military service. (2) A full homestead property tax exemption exists only for former Prisoners of War who also have a total (100%) service-connected disability, under Article X, Section 6 of the Missouri Constitution. A broader constitutional amendment that would have created a tiered/full property tax exemption for disabled veterans generally (proportional to VA rating, full exemption at higher ratings) has repeatedly failed to pass the Missouri legislature as of mid-2026 (reported by local news as failing for an 8th consecutive year in the 2026 session) and could not be confirmed as enacted law against any official source in this session; claims on non-official veteran-benefit aggregator sites that this expansion took effect January 1, 2026 are NOT confirmed and are presented here as unverified/likely inaccurate.
findings.value: Up to $1,100/year credit (homeowners) or $750/year credit (renters) for 100% disabled veterans within income limits; full homestead exemption only for former POWs with total service-connected disability
otherReqs: 100% VA service-connected disability rating (for the Property Tax Credit)
Household income within program limits
For the POW exemption: former Prisoner of War status AND 100% service-connected disability AND owner-occupied primary residence
findings.agency: Missouri Department of Revenue (Property Tax Credit); County Assessor (POW homestead exemption)
documentation: VA letter confirming 100% service-connected disability rating
For POW exemption: DD-214 showing POW status or letter from Military Personnel Records Center/VA, plus VA letter confirming total service-connected disability
findings.legalCitation: Mo. Const. art. X, § 6 (POW homestead exemption); Property Tax Credit program administered under Chapter 135, RSMo
findings.sourceExcerpt: Renters: 'your total household income must be $27,200 or less' (single) / '$29,200 or less' (married). Full-year homeowners: 'your total household income must be $30,000 or less' (single) / '$34,000 or less' (married). Veteran benefits are included in household income calculations 'unless the claimant or spouse is a 100 percent disabled as a result of military service.'

findings.name: Missouri Veterans Homes
findings.description: Missouri operates seven state veterans homes (Cameron, Cape Girardeau, Mexico, Mt. Vernon, St. James, St. Louis, and Warrensburg) managing a combined 1,238 beds for long-term skilled nursing care. Eligibility requires valid veteran status per VA standards, a need for 24-hour skilled nursing care, Missouri residency of 180 consecutive days prior to application, no sex-offender registry listing, and no Class A or B felony convictions. The 2026 monthly rate is $2,773, covering medical care, 24-hour nursing, physician oversight, therapies, medication management, meals, and recreational activities.
findings.value: Skilled nursing and long-term care; 2026 monthly rate of $2,773
otherReqs: Valid veteran status per VA standards
Requires 24-hour skilled nursing care
180 consecutive days of Missouri residency prior to application
No sex offender registry listing
No Class A or B felony convictions in any state
documentation: Durable Power of Attorney paperwork (if applicable)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Missouri operates 7 Veterans Homes across the state located in Cameron, Cape Girardeau, Mexico, Mt. Vernon, St. James, St. Louis, and Warrensburg. The system manages 1,238 beds for long-term skilled nursing care. The 2026 monthly rate is $2,773.

findings.name: Missouri Returning Heroes' Education Act
findings.description: Combat veterans (those who served in an armed combat zone since September 11, 2001, honorably discharged, and a Missouri resident/registered voter) attending Missouri public institutions of higher education have tuition capped at $50 per credit hour for undergraduate certificate, associate, or baccalaureate programs, provided they maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 on a 4.0 scale. For graduate degree programs (master's and doctorate; professional degrees like law, medicine, and veterinary medicine are excluded), tuition is capped at no more than 30% of the cost of tuition and fees. Undergraduate eligibility lasts 10 years from the veteran's last discharge; graduate eligibility lasts 20 years.
findings.value: $50/credit hour tuition cap (undergraduate); tuition capped at 30% of cost (graduate)
otherReqs: Served in an armed combat zone since September 11, 2001, documented via DD-214, combat service medals, or imminent danger/hostile fire pay
Honorably discharged
Missouri resident or registered/eligible Missouri voter
Maintain 2.5 CGPA (undergraduate)
Enrolled in a Missouri public institution
Professional degree programs (law, medicine, veterinary) excluded from the graduate rate cap
findings.agency: Missouri Department of Higher Education & Workforce Development
documentation: DD-214 or other documentation of combat service
findings.sourceExcerpt: Public institutions receiving state funds must cap tuition at $50 per credit hour for combat veterans pursuing certificates or associate/baccalaureate degrees, provided they maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 on a 4-point scale... For graduate degree programs, institutions must limit tuition to no more than thirty percent of the cost of tuition and fees.

findings.name: State Employment Veterans Preference
findings.description: Under Missouri's Merit System law, veterans, disabled veterans, surviving spouses of veterans, and spouses of disabled veterans are given preference in state employment: preference in appointment over other eligibles when relevant job-related factors are otherwise equal, and appropriate credit toward competitive examinations for related military training or experience. The statute as directly read this session (RSMo 36.220) describes a qualitative "preference when equally qualified" and experience-credit mechanism rather than a specific numeric point system. Several non-official veteran benefit sites describe this as a 5-point preference for veterans and 10-point preference for disabled veterans, but that specific point allocation could not be confirmed against the official statute text or any Missouri Office of Administration page reached in this session, so it is not presented as confirmed fact.
findings.value: Preference in state hiring for veterans, disabled veterans, and qualifying spouses when candidates are otherwise equally qualified; credit for related military training/experience in exams
otherReqs: Honorable discharge
Also extends to surviving spouses of veterans and spouses of disabled veterans
findings.agency: Missouri Office of Administration, Division of Personnel
documentation: VA disability rating letter (for disabled veteran preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: veterans, disabled veterans, surviving spouses and spouses of disabled veterans shall be given preference [in competitive examinations]... a veteran, or the surviving spouse of a veteran, a disabled veteran, or the spouse of a disabled veteran shall be given preference in appointment over other eligibles if all other relevant job-related factors are equal.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
findings.description: Missouri residents honorably discharged from the U.S. Armed Forces with any VA-documented service-connected disability (no minimum percentage specified) may obtain one set of Disabled Veteran license plates at no cost, including no specialty plate, transfer, processing, or replacement fees, and no personalization fee if a personalized configuration is chosen. Standard Disabled Veteran plates do not confer disabled-parking privileges unless the plate also displays the wheelchair accessibility symbol, which requires an additional physician's statement (Form DOR-1776) confirming a permanent disability.
findings.value: One set of Disabled Veteran license plates free of charge (no specialty, transfer, processing, replacement, or personalization fees)
otherReqs: Honorably discharged from the U.S. Armed Forces
VA statement (no more than one year old) confirming a service-connected disability, issued directly by the VA (not a hospital or clinic)
Wheelchair accessibility symbol (for disabled parking privileges) requires a separate physician's statement confirming permanent disability
findings.agency: Missouri Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Bureau
documentation: Form 4601 (Application for Missouri Military Personalized License Plates)
VA statement confirming service-connected disability, issued within the last year
Form DOR-1776 (Physician's Statement) if requesting the wheelchair accessibility symbol
findings.sourceExcerpt: An eligible applicant may obtain one free set of Disabled Veteran license plate(s)... A statement from the United States Department of Veteran Affairs, no more than one year old, stating your disability is service-connected [is required]. The letter must be directly from the VA, not a veteran's hospital or clinic.

findings.name: Sales Tax Exemption for Vehicle Modification/Adaptive Equipment
findings.description: Missouri exempts from state and local sales/use tax items used solely to modify a motor vehicle to permit its use by an individual with a disability (e.g., hand controls, wheelchair lifts, ramps, modified accelerator/brake systems), under RSMo 144.030.2(18). This applies to disabled individuals generally, including disabled veterans, rather than being a veteran-exclusive benefit. Multiple non-official veteran benefit sites also claim Missouri exempts 100% disabled veterans from sales tax on an entire motor vehicle purchase once every three years; this broader vehicle-purchase exemption could not be confirmed against the Missouri Department of Revenue's official sales/use tax exemption list or statute 144.030 in this session, and is not included here as a confirmed benefit.
findings.value: Sales/use tax exemption on items used solely to modify a vehicle for use by a person with a disability
otherReqs: Modification items must be used solely to permit vehicle use by an individual with a disability
Documentation showing vehicle and equipment priced separately
documentation: Invoice or documentation showing vehicle and adaptive equipment priced separately
findings.sourceExcerpt: Items used solely to modify motor vehicles to permit the use of such motor vehicles by individuals with disabilities [are exempt from sales tax] under section 144.030.2(18).

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting and Fishing Permit Exemption
findings.description: Honorably discharged Missouri resident or nonresident veterans with a service-related disability of 60% or greater (or former prisoners of war) may hunt without a permit (excluding black bears, deer, elk, and turkeys, and trapping is not covered) and fish without a permit (a trout permit/trout park tag is still required), provided they carry a certified statement of eligibility from the VA. Waterfowl, snipe, doves, woodcock, and rails still require a Missouri Migratory Bird Hunting Permit, and a Federal Duck Stamp is still required for waterfowl.
findings.value: Free hunting (excluding black bear/deer/elk/turkey, no trapping) and fishing (excluding trout permit) without a state permit
otherReqs: Honorably discharged
60%+ service-related disability, or former POW status
Must carry a certified statement of eligibility from the VA while hunting/fishing
Deer, turkey, elk, black bear, and migratory birds still require separate permits/stamps
documentation: Certified statement of eligibility from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs noting the 60%+ service-connected rating
findings.sourceExcerpt: 60% or greater [service-related disability qualifies veterans for permit exemptions]... Applicants must carry a certified statement of eligibility from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.

findings.name: Military Retirement Pay Income Tax Exemption
findings.description: Missouri fully exempts military retirement/retired pay from state income tax. Veterans subtract their total military retirement benefits (as reported on federal Form 1040/1040-SR, Line 5b) from Missouri adjusted gross income, entered on Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 10, and included in total subtractions on Form MO-1040. This full subtraction applies to tax years 2021 and forward (prior years used a phased exemption claimed on Form MO-A, Part 3, Section D). Note: Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) annuity payments do not qualify for this specific military pension subtraction, though they may qualify for Missouri's separate public pension exemption. This benefit is distinct from VA disability compensation, which is already exempt from both federal and Missouri income tax as a matter of federal law.
findings.value: Full exemption of military retirement/retired pay from Missouri state income tax
otherReqs: Applies to military retired pay reported on federal Form 1040/1040-SR Line 5b
Claimed via Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 10 for tax years 2021 and later
Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) annuity payments do not qualify under this subtraction (may qualify under the general public pension exemption instead)
documentation: Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR showing military retirement benefits on Line 5b
findings.sourceExcerpt: Your total military retirement benefits reported on federal Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR, Line 5b may be subtracted from your federal adjusted gross income. The military pension must be entered on Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 10... The Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) annuity does not qualify for the military pension subtraction but may qualify for the public pension exemption instead.
